gitCommit.subject: The approval card shows the rules that decided, and lets you change them there (#360)
gitCommit.body:
The approval card shows the rules that decided, and lets you change them there (#360)

* The approval card shows the rules that decided, and lets you change them there

On 2026-09-21 an owner answered "Always for this server"; the rule was written,
an Everyone rule naming the exact tool kept asking, and the card said nothing.
The precedence was right. It was simply invisible.

The order is now a value, not a `.find()` ladder: `explainApprovalRules` returns
every rule matching one call, most specific first, the winner marked, and
`matchApprovalRule` derives its answer from that list. One truth.

The card shows that list, and a rule changes only through its own line. No
"Always" button writes a rule as a side effect of answering any more. The one
grant left on the card is narrower than any of them: "Approve for this project"
auto-approves this tool for this agent WHILE IT WORKS IN THIS FOLDER, via
`approval_rules.condition_json` (no migration, the column was already there).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review pass 1: nothing widens a folder-scoped rule in silence

Seven findings from Reviewer C, three of them important.

A rule confined to a folder could be turned into a global grant without a word:
the card's "Change" line dropped the condition, and both Yolo toggles overwrote
it. "Change" now carries the folder through, and any GLOBAL auto_approve over a
folder-scoped rule is refused by name. Only the permissive direction is refused;
restricting still clears the condition, which takes a permission away.

A request with no agent showed "Tool default" as the winner while an Everyone
rule was in fact deciding: the exact lie #346 closes. It now reads the Everyone
tiers through a sentinel id no rule can carry.

A conditioned rule no longer jumps ahead of every tier. It sorts first inside
its own tier, which is the same thing where it matters (agent + exact tool is
already the top tier) and closes a privilege escalation: a conditioned wildcard
beat an explicit `block`.

Also: a re-read that cannot find its request says so instead of keeping a stale
chain; `C:` and `D:` stop normalising to the same empty string; the dead
`mcpRulePattern` field is gone; the MCP ambiguity warning is in English.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Review pass 2 minors: the guard holds its row, and a UNC path stays its own place

Reviewer C approved the pass, with two minor findings.

The folder-rule guard read the row and wrote outside any shared transaction, so
two concurrent gestures could both pass it and the second would overwrite the
folder rule with a global grant. The guard now runs inside the caller's
transaction and takes the row `FOR UPDATE`, in all three writers.

`normaliseWorkspacePath` collapsed a UNC path onto a POSIX one: `\server\share`
and `/server/share` are not the same place, and the two leading slashes are now
kept.

Also renames the component in comments that still pointed at the deleted
`ApprovalActions`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
